corrections.text: The article says none of the cited sources reports "scores from a judge other than Grok 4.7"; the sentence concerns scores for Arete-27B, and none of the cited sources reports any. The Decoder's report of 2026-11-01 does describe scores from a different judge (GPT-5.6 Luna) in the Vals AI study, but for other models and on a different scale. It also says Thomson 1.0 Small, a model Thomson Reuters fine-tuned from Qwen3.6 35B, adopted official Chinese government positions less often in Vals's testing than the original model (84.6 percent versus 15.0 percent, as The Decoder reports it); that result does not concern Arete-27B.

The article says the pages it cites do not say whether the "private China censorship eval" (1,111 prompts) in the training-data release manifest is the published 803-prompt set. The training-data card was edited at 21:14 UTC on 2026-11-06 to replace "a private eval" and "all 1,111 eval prompts" with a link to Propaganda_Eval and "all eval prompts"; the release manifest still carries the original wording and number, and no cited page states the size of the set the card now links.

The article says the model card's three edits after its first full version "renamed the linked evaluation ... and trimmed the release descriptions". The edits of 20:51 and 20:53 UTC did so; the third (21:04 UTC) only added the `datasets` and `base_model` (Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B) fields to the card metadata. The evaluation dataset's own history records a commit "Rename to Propaganda_Eval; trim README" at 20:24 UTC.
